pool.text: Altan Khan began building the Da Zhao Temple on the Tümed plain.
The Ming changed Kokegota's name to Guihua representing naturalization.
Ligdan Khan completely razed the city of Guihua during attacks.
Hui merchants gathered north of the fortress gate building a mosque.
The Qing supervised southwestern Inner Mongolia defense from garrison town Suiyuan.
French missionaries established a Catholic church in the city of Guihua.
A bubonic plague outbreak occurred affecting the town of Guisui.
The transportation line began operation in the area.
Guisui was chosen as the regional administrative centre replacing Zhangjiakou.
The city was renamed from Guisui to Hohhot officially.
An expressway linked Hohhot with Baotou known as Hubao Expressway.
The city's far east side began development into government buildings.
Hohhot was declared Dairy Capital of China by associations.
Hohhot was connected to northern counties by the Huwu Highway.
The Hohhot City Stadium on the north side was finished.
Construction of a high-speed railway station began following plans.
The high-speed railway station was completed and serviced ordinary lines.
Hohhot achieved a GDP of RMB 247.56 billion.
CRH opened its first D-series route in Inner Mongolia corridor.
The section between Hohhot and Ulanqab opened for travel.
